content.text:
Yes: **channel X(0) is intended to inherit global**, and adding `fully_quantise_mask == 0` inside the existing inheritance clause is the smallest targeted fix. One qualification: **explicit step X currently bypasses the channel default; clearing the step restores channel inheritance**—the proposed fix preserves that distinction.

- **Contract/UI:** [device_map.lua:275](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/devices/device_map.lua:275) defines `off_value = 0`, range `0–2`, labels `X/OFF/ON`. [param_manager.lua:69](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/devices/param_manager.lua:69) initializes the stock default from that sentinel. [README.md:838](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/README.md:838) describes channel/step overrides of global quantisation. History supports a sentinel mismatch: commit `a317edb1` changed the domain from `-1…1` to `0…2`; `a5e3412a` retained inheritance checks for `nil/-1`.
- **Cause:** [step.lua:38](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/step.lua:38) returns assigned channel `0` directly, whereas unassigned default `0` resolves to `nil`. [step.lua:811](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/step.lua:811) recognizes only `nil/-1` as inherited. Adding zero changes only resolved-zero cases with global ON; explicit OFF(1), ON(2), and global OFF retain their behavior.
- **Native evidence:** [results.json:504](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-runs/6dae16456cc943e8a5ff19c749834399/results.json:504) records successful global quantisation; subsequent results confirm channel OFF and step ON. The [manifest:23](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-runs/6dae16456cc943e8a5ff19c749834399/manifest.json:23) records OFF→X failing with `[60,65,69,71]` instead of `[62,65,71,60]`. This is native **controlled-experimental, diagnostic-only** evidence, not an admitted timing pass. Assertions after [mask_quantisation.py:69](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/tests/behaviour/mask_quantisation.py:69) were not reached.
- **Side effects:** The boolean also feeds masked chord/arp processing through [step.lua:634](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/step.lua:634), so inherited global ON should change those voices consistently. Ordinary unmasked pitch processing and fixed-note precedence remain unchanged. Keep the adjustment local; it provides no basis to broaden Digitakt NRPN allowances or generic parameter resolution.

Recommended regression matrix below shows **full quantisation enabled**, not whether ordinary scale snapping occurs. `G` means the global setting; execute every row with global OFF and ON.

| Assignment / channel value | No step lock | Explicit step X(0) | Step OFF(1) | Step ON(2) | After step clear |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Unassigned / X | G | N/A | N/A | N/A | G |
| Unassigned / OFF | OFF | N/A | N/A | N/A | OFF |
| Unassigned / ON | ON | N/A | N/A | N/A | ON |
| Assigned / X | G | G | OFF | ON | G |
| Assigned / OFF | OFF | G | OFF | ON | OFF |
| Assigned / ON | ON | G | OFF | ON | ON |

Explicit step X returns `nil` immediately at [step.lua:46](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/step.lua:46); clear removes the lock at [program.lua:566](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/models/program.lua:566). Thus X and clear must be tested separately. If step X should instead inherit the channel, that is an additional contract change this one-line fix does not implement.

Exercise fresh assignment plus OFF→X and ON→X; clear each step state using held-step K2 and channel-wide K1+K2 on **Trig Locks**. Assert preserved defaults and unaffected neighboring channels. Use the existing degree/rotation pitch fixture, repeat with snapping disabled and an accidental, and include one masked chord/arp case plus an unmasked control; retain velocity, duration and event-count assertions.

**CONFIDENCE: High** for the targeted fix; it remains proposed and untested. No edits or launches performed; an explicit contract requiring step X to equal clear would expand the required change.
